boundary: Finite synthetic same-owner software, mathematical and documentation evidence only. No real process, person, participant, observation, measurement, system, identity, credential, deployment, professional judgment, legal or cultural conclusion, affected-party or Maori authority, empirical GMUT confirmation, production THOS or Freed ID, complete privacy or accessibility assurance, exhaustive security, independent reproduction, AGI or ASI, consciousness, personhood, Theory-of-Everything proof, canon, or Stage 20 readiness.

hypotheses.name: Evidence Conservation
hypotheses.statement: Claims may not exceed attributable evidence after transformation.

hypotheses.name: Correction Nonerasure
hypotheses.statement: A recovery does not erase the failed subject that caused it.

hypotheses.name: Authority Separation
hypotheses.statement: Operational permission, scientific truth, and affected-party authority are distinct.

hypotheses.name: Reversibility Budget
hypotheses.statement: Higher-impact actions require stronger rollback and state readback.

hypotheses.name: Uncertainty Monotonicity
hypotheses.statement: Unmeasured uncertainty cannot be reduced by relabeling.

hypotheses.name: Provenance Entropy
hypotheses.statement: Each undocumented transformation increases reconstruction uncertainty.

hypotheses.name: Boundary Nonpromotion
hypotheses.statement: A finite synthetic pass cannot promote an empirical or universal claim.

hypotheses.name: Consent Precedence
hypotheses.statement: Affected-party consent precedes benefit claims about those parties.

hypotheses.name: Resource Honesty
hypotheses.statement: Workload counts cannot substitute for semantic novelty or evidence quality.

hypotheses.name: Observer Declaration
hypotheses.statement: Every reported result declares the observer, frame, and byte domain.

hypotheses.name: Counterfactual Symmetry
hypotheses.statement: Equivalent relabelings preserve only explicitly proven invariants.

hypotheses.name: Care Before Deployment
hypotheses.statement: Safety, rollback, accessibility, and governance precede live deployment.

hypotheses.name: Pluralism Under Constraint
hypotheses.statement: Multiple interpretations remain until evidence rules them out.

hypotheses.name: Accessible Reservation
hypotheses.statement: Structural accessibility checks reserve rather than replace user evaluation.

hypotheses.name: Terminal Latch
hypotheses.statement: A successful exact-final canonical closes replay unless a new exact final exists.
